title: Braiding the Money: WIOA, AIF, RSI, CAI, and the GI Bill
description: Who pays for what in an apprenticeship? This course maps every California and federal stream that can fund an apprentice or a program, the rules that prevent double-billing, and the sequence for stacking them. Includes a one-page braiding worksheet.
notes: Audience: Case managers, business services, program managers. Format: LV. Hours assumed from format (LV = 3 hours). Gap addressed: 44 percent of practitioners cannot say who pays for each component; no California document maps these streams for frontline staff.
learning_objectives: Match each apprenticeship component (OJT, related instruction, supportive services, program development) to its eligible funding sources.
Apply the no-double-dip rules, such as RSI hours not claimable when funded by a CAI grant.
Calculate an AIF-supported funding scenario for a sample apprentice.
Identify when GI Bill OJT and apprenticeship benefits apply and how the housing allowance steps down.

sequencing_rationale: Lessons follow the catalog's learning objectives in the order a practitioner meets them on the job: Mapping Components to Funding Sources; No-Double-Dip Rules; Calculating an AIF Scenario; GI Bill OJT and Apprenticeship Benefits. The closing project ("Project: Complete the Braiding Worksheet") applies the earlier lessons to one realistic work product (a completed braiding worksheet for a sample apprentice that assigns each component to an eligible source with no double-billing) rather than introducing new content. Scope assumptions: hours are not stated in the source catalog and are assumed from the delivery format (LV; LV = 3 hours). Content is grounded in California and federal guidance named in the catalog description and objectives; the course cites those directives by number but does not reproduce their text, and every policy-specific claim must be checked against the current directive before delivery. Local board policy is treated as a variable the learner fills in from their own board, not something the course prescribes. Design driver (catalog "gap addressed"): 44 percent of practitioners cannot say who pays for each component; no California document maps these streams for frontline staff. Statistics and audit findings quoted from the catalog have not been independently verified. Prerequisites reflect track order: APP 101 (Registered Apprenticeship for Workforce Professionals).
